B: Which statement best describes a nuclear-encoded mitochondrial matrix enzyme?
Its mRNA must be translated by mitochondrial ribosomes
It is generally synthesized in the cytosol and imported
It passes through the Golgi before entering mitochondria
It is encoded by mitochondrial DNA

Nuclear-encoded mitochondrial matrix proteins normally originate from cytosolic translation. The mitochondrial genome supplies only a subset of mitochondrial proteins. The ordinary matrix route does not pass through the Golgi.
The most direct function of a targeting signal is to:
Increase the number of peptide bonds
Specify interactions that help direct cargo to a destination
Act as an RNA polymerase promoter
A targeting signal is interpreted at the protein level by cellular recognition factors. It does not independently dictate translation, transcription or stability.
A typical classical nuclear localization signal contains:
Lysine and arginine are characteristic of many classical NLSs. SKL is a canonical PTS1. The hydrophobic ER signal normally engages a different route.
Which component directly recognizes the cargo NLS in the classical importin α/β pathway?
Importin α is the classical NLS-binding adaptor; importin β interacts with the pore. RCC1 and RanGAP control the nucleotide state of Ran.
Chromatin-associated RCC1 promotes nucleotide exchange on nuclear Ran. This spatial localization supports high nuclear Ran-GTP.
What is a typical role of nuclear Ran-GTP in classical protein import?
Cleaves the NLS from every cargo
Promotes disassembly of the import complex
Ran-GTP binding to importin β helps disassemble the import complex in the nucleus. Cargo release does not normally involve NLS cleavage.
Which statement about CRM1-mediated protein export is correct?
Ran-GTP supports export complex assembly in the nucleus
Ran-GDP drives binding to a thylakoid receptor
The NES must be cleaved in cytosol
For CRM1-mediated export, Ran-GTP cooperates with NES-bearing cargo in the nucleus, and hydrolysis promotes release in cytoplasm. This differs from import-complex assembly.
The selective central barrier of the nuclear pore is strongly associated with:
FG-rich nucleoporins interact with transport receptors and contribute to selective passage. The other components do not constitute the pore barrier.
Which is a typical feature of a mitochondrial matrix-targeting presequence?
An amino-terminal amphipathic, positively charged sequence
A typical mitochondrial presequence presents hydrophobic and basic faces and is often cleaved. It is not the same as a PTS1 or a thylakoid Tat signal.
Which is a major channel of the outer mitochondrial membrane import apparatus?
Tom40 is the channel component of TOM. Pex7 recognizes PTS2, Toc75 belongs to plastid outer-envelope import, and Sec61 belongs to ER translocation.
For typical presequence-bearing matrix cargo, which sequence of systems is appropriate?
The cargo first crosses the outer mitochondrial membrane through TOM, then engages the inner-membrane presequence machinery and associated ATP-dependent matrix motor.
MPP commonly removes the matrix-targeting extension. Its activity is distinct from the translocases and from the peroxisomal recycling machinery.
Many mitochondrial inner-membrane metabolite carriers use which route?
TOM, small TIM chaperones and TIM22
The carrier route commonly uses internal targeting information, small TIM chaperones and TIM22. It need not use a cleavable amino-terminal presequence.
What normally distinguishes the electrical state across the mitochondrial inner membrane?
The matrix must be positive for presequence import
There is no potential during normal respiration
The outer membrane provides the same principal driving potential
The matrix-negative inner-membrane potential favors entry of positive groups in typical presequences. The outer membrane is not the analogous energized barrier.
Which chloroplast enzyme commonly removes an envelope-targeting transit peptide?
SPP processes many imported stromal precursors. Mitochondrial processing peptidase acts in the mitochondrial pathway; the other choices are regulatory or recycling factors.
Which chloroplast components are associated with early receptor function?
The canonical TOC receptor machinery includes Toc34 and Toc159-family GTPases. The other pairs belong to distinct import systems.
Which route transports suitable folded proteins across the thylakoid membrane?
The twin-arginine pathway can transport folded substrates and uses the thylakoid proton motive force. TOM/TIM belong to mitochondria, CRM1 to nuclear export.
The ordinary envelope import of a soluble chloroplast precursor generally involves:
TOC and TIC with GTP- and ATP-dependent contributions
Only a mitochondrial-style matrix-negative electrical potential
TOC receptor GTPases and stromal ATP-dependent assistance support the canonical route. The thylakoid gradient and mitochondrial inner-membrane potential are distinct.
Which signal is normally retained at the extreme carboxyl terminus of a PTS1 cargo?
PTS1 is commonly a retained carboxyl-terminal motif. ER, mitochondrial and plastid amino-terminal signals are distinct, and classical NLSs are not defined by terminal SKL.
PEX7 is the PTS2 receptor. PEX5 recognizes PTS1 and may act as a coreceptor for PTS2 in some organisms.
Which proteins participate in ATP-dependent Pex5 receptor extraction?
Pex1/Pex6 AAA ATPases drive receptor recycling. The other pairs have different recognition or nucleotide-regulatory functions.
Which statement about the site of synthesis of secretory and organelle proteins is most accurate?
Each destination has a dedicated cytosolic ribosome species
Cytosolic ribosomes can produce both classes, with targeting directing their fate
All proteins are translated within their final destination
All peroxisomal proteins are translated in the ER lumen
The same cytosolic ribosome population can synthesize different classes of cargo. Nascent-chain targeting can recruit ribosomes to the ER; peroxisomes lack their own translation machinery.
Assertion: Nuclear import can deliver folded proteins. Reason: A soluble receptor-bound cargo can pass through a selective aqueous nuclear pore.
Both true; reason does not explain assertion
Nuclear pores permit receptor-mediated transport of folded macromolecules without obligatory threading through a membrane-spanning narrow-chain translocon. The reason explains the assertion.
Assertion: Canonical PTS1 cargo usually retains its signal. Reason: PTS1 is a terminal recognition motif that need not be excised after cargo delivery.
Both true; reason does not explain assertion
The common PTS1 is a noncleaved terminal signal; removal is not an obligatory step for delivery, unlike many mitochondrial or plastid transit peptides.
Assertion: Proteins in the mitochondrial matrix are all encoded by mitochondrial DNA. Reason: Mitochondria possess their own genome.
Both true; reason does not explain assertion
Mitochondrial DNA exists, but most mitochondrial protein species are nuclear encoded. A correct observation about the organelle's genome does not imply complete autonomy.
Assertion: A processed mitochondrial precursor must always be fully imported. Reason: The targeting extension can emerge into the matrix before the rest of the chain.
Both true; reason does not explain assertion
Processing can precede completion of translocation. The reason demonstrates why the assertion is false.
Assertion: The chloroplast Tat pathway and mitochondrial TIM23 use identical transport mechanisms. Reason: The Tat pathway can transport folded proteins using the thylakoid proton motive force.
Both true; reason does not explain assertion
The reason correctly describes Tat. TIM23 normally accommodates an extended precursor with a distinct electrical and ATP-dependent mechanism.
Consider I: PTS1 is commonly C-terminal. II: Classical NLSs are usually cleaved. III: A stromal transit peptide is commonly N-terminal. IV: All mitochondrial proteins use TIM23. Which are correct?
I and III describe typical signals. Classical NLSs generally remain, and carrier, outer-membrane and intermembrane-space routes prevent universal assignment to TIM23.
Match 1 importin β, 2 Tom40, 3 Toc75, 4 Pex5 with a PTS1 recognition, b nuclear pore interactions, c outer mitochondrial channel, d outer plastid channel.
Importin β mediates pore interactions, Tom40 and Toc75 are channel components of distinct outer membranes, and Pex5 recognizes PTS1.

Which statements correctly describe experimental evidence? I: Colocalization can suggest destination. II: Protease protection alone always proves matrix localization. III: A signal-transfer fusion can test sufficiency. IV: Reduced total abundance necessarily proves failed translation.
I and III are correct. Protection depends on which membrane shields the protein; abundance reflects synthesis, degradation and other fates. Neither II nor IV is generally valid.
C: experimental interpretation

A 75-kDa reporter is cytosolic alone, nuclear when fused to a candidate sequence, and cytosolic when the candidate's key lysines are replaced. All constructs have equal abundance. What conclusion is strongest?
The signal is sufficient in this reporter and its basic residues contribute
Every native protein with a lysine cluster uses importin α
RCC1 must directly bind the signal
The reporter was translated in the nucleus

The gain-of-function fusion and the mutation support signal-dependent localization under the tested conditions. They do not identify the receptor without binding or perturbation evidence, or show nuclear translation.
experimental interpretation
An NLS cargo binds importin α normally, but a mutation prevents association of α with β. Which early phenotype is most plausible?
Normal classical pore passage and failed peptide cleavage
Selective impairment of efficient receptor-mediated passage
Increased mitochondrial membrane potential
Unchanged transport because α must always act alone
Cargo recognition survives but recruitment of the pore-interacting β subunit is defective. Classical import is therefore impaired despite intact NLS binding.
experimental interpretation
Nuclear Ran-GTP enrichment falls following a defect in nuclear RCC1. Which paired change is expected?
Both cargo import and export necessarily accelerate
Only Golgi transport is affected
Import-complex release and CRM1 export-complex formation are impaired
Pex5 monoubiquitination necessarily stops
Nuclear Ran-GTP normally favors import-complex disassembly and CRM1 export-complex formation. Reducing it disrupts both steps; effects on unrelated machinery are not established.
analytical
A factor accumulates in nuclei after signaling, but total protein is unchanged. Which observation best distinguishes faster import from slower export?
A single endpoint image
The genomic sequence alone
A measurement of total DNA
Time-resolved import and export measurements under controlled conditions
Both kinetic changes can produce the same steady-state distribution. Separately tracking influx and efflux helps resolve the mechanism; endpoint localization cannot.
numerical
Hypothetical shuttling cargo has k_in = 0.24 min⁻¹ and k_out = 0.06 min⁻¹. Under the two-pool model, what is its steady-state nuclear fraction?
At steady state the fraction is k_in/(k_in+k_out) = 0.24/0.30 = 0.80. The ratio N/C is 4, not the fraction. This assumes no synthesis or degradation and first-order exchange.
numerical
A nucleus contains 300 labelled molecules in 100 µm³, while cytosol contains 900 in 600 µm³. What is the nuclear-to-cytosolic concentration ratio?
The nuclear concentration is 300/100 = 3 molecules/µm³; cytosol is 900/600 = 1.5 molecules/µm³. The ratio is 2. The number ratio 1/3 is not the concentration ratio.
experimental interpretation
A mitochondrial precursor is processed to a shorter form, but the mature-sized band is destroyed by protease added to intact mitochondria. Markers confirm membrane integrity. What is justified?
Complete matrix import is established
The precursor is necessarily translated in mitochondria
Processing occurred, but complete protected delivery is not established
All mitochondrial membrane proteins are absent
The band shift supports processing; external protease sensitivity demonstrates accessibility and prevents concluding complete protected import. An intermediate could have an exposed region.
experimental interpretation
Protein X resists protease in intact mitochondria, becomes sensitive after outer-membrane disruption, and matrix markers remain protected. X is soluble. Which compartment is most consistent?
Cytosol
Matrix
Nucleus
Intermembrane space

The outer membrane protected X but the intact inner membrane still protects matrix markers. A soluble intermembrane-space location is the most consistent; membrane association would need additional checks for nonsoluble substrates.
experimental interpretation
The same mitochondrial presequence-DHFR fusion is imported in one sample but fails when a ligand stabilizes DHFR. An unrelated matrix cargo imports normally. What is best supported?
A stable fold can obstruct import of the tested substrate
The ligand destroys all mitochondria
The presequence is absent from the inhibited construct
All protein import requires unfolding

The signal and organelle are controlled; the cargo's ligand-stabilized fold is the relevant difference. The result supports a conformational barrier in this route, not a general block of all organelle import.
numerical
For an idealized +2 charge crossing Δψ = −0.120 V into the mitochondrial matrix, estimate zFΔψ with F = 96,485 C mol⁻¹.
−11.6 kJ/mol
−23.2 kJ/mol
+23.2 kJ/mol
−231.6 kJ/mol
2 × 96,485 × (−0.120) = −23,156.4 J/mol, or approximately −23.2 kJ/mol. The sign represents a favorable electrical contribution, not total import free energy.
numerical
In an ideal first-order import assay with k = 0.10 min⁻¹, what fraction is imported after 10 min?
f = 1 − e^(−kt) = 1 − e^(−1) ≈ 0.632. The remaining fraction is 0.368. This assumes a wholly competent pool and negligible competing loss.
experimental interpretation
A TIM22-specific defect strongly impairs a multi-pass mitochondrial carrier but a standard matrix preprotein remains imported. Which interpretation is most coherent?
All mitochondrial proteins use TIM22
TOM is completely absent
Nuclear export has stopped
Different cargo classes use different inner-membrane sorting pathways
The carrier commonly uses TIM22 whereas the classical matrix protein uses TIM23/PAM. Preserved matrix import argues against generalized failure of all mitochondrial import.
experimental interpretation

A mitochondrion imports a matrix protein in the normal condition. A mutant produces a full-length band that is protease protected even after selective outer-membrane disruption. A matrix marker remains protected. What should be examined next?
The processing peptidase or its cleavage site
Whether SKL is at the C terminus
Nuclear Ran-GTP hydrolysis
Thylakoid proton gradient

The full-length protein appears protected by the inner membrane despite absent processing. A processing defect is a plausible explanation, although internal localization and cleavage should be confirmed by independent evidence.
experimental interpretation
A chloroplast precursor binds the outer envelope normally in a mutant, yet no protected stromal product forms. Which inference is most defensible?
The transit peptide is definitely missing
A post-recognition import or processing step may be defective
Every TOC receptor has disappeared
The precursor must be a mitochondrial protein

Normal association argues that at least some recognition remains. Failure after that point could involve transfer, translocation, energy or processing. The exact mutated component cannot be identified from these observations alone.
experimental interpretation
An otherwise functional chloroplast lumen precursor has an intact envelope transit peptide but its second Tat-targeting signal is disrupted. What is the expected primary defect?
It is never synthesized
It passes into the ER lumen
It reaches stroma but is impaired in delivery to thylakoid lumen
It must be delivered to the mitochondrial matrix
The first signal can direct envelope entry; the disrupted second signal impairs internal targeting. Accumulation or degradation of the stromal intermediate depends on the system.
experimental interpretation

Two chloroplast preparations import the same stromal reporter normally. Only the preparation with intact thylakoid proton motive force delivers a Tat-dependent reporter into the lumen. What is supported?
Envelope transport requires the mitochondrial presequence potential
The stromal reporter must be Tat dependent
The nuclear pore is defective
The thylakoid gradient is important for the specified second transport step
The stromal control establishes that envelope transport remains competent. The selective effect is consistent with Tat's dependence on the thylakoid proton motive force.
experimental interpretation
A chloroplast precursor becomes a smaller intermediate protected in intact chloroplasts but sensitive after envelope rupture, while lumenal markers remain protected. What is the best explanation?
The intermediate is consistent with stromal localization rather than lumenal delivery
The intermediate must be cytosolic
The intermediate must be inside the thylakoid lumen
The protein never encountered a processing enzyme

Envelope integrity explains protection; once it is removed the protein is accessible while lumen markers remain protected. Processing plus protection supports an internal intermediate, not completion of the second step.
experimental interpretation
A folded reporter ending in SKL localizes to peroxisomal matrix. Adding a bulky tag after SKL disrupts localization despite similar protein abundance. Which mechanism is most consistent?
The reporter no longer contains serine
The terminal position or accessibility needed for PEX5 recognition is disrupted
The tag abolishes all organelle ATP synthesis
The signal has become an NLS
PTS1 recognition depends on the extreme carboxyl-terminal presentation. The sequence is still present but its functional context changed. Equal abundance helps exclude a simple synthesis difference.
experimental interpretation
In a peroxisomal mutant, Pex5 binds PTS1 cargo normally and reaches the membrane, but accumulates there; sustained import falls. Which class of defect is most consistent?
Cytosolic ribosome initiation only
Nuclear export via CRM1
ATP-dependent Pex5 extraction/recycling
Deletion of the cargo's SKL motif
Recognition and docking are observed; recycling is the likely downstream problem. Pex1/Pex6 or associated steps should be investigated rather than claiming a specific gene from localization alone.
analytical
A mammalian PEX7-deficient cell imports a standard PTS1 reporter efficiently but fails to import a validated PTS2 reporter. Which interpretation fits?
Pex7 is the common PTS1 receptor
All peroxisomal matrix import has ceased
PEX7 is required for TOM
The PTS2 recognition route is selectively disrupted
PEX7 recognizes PTS2. PTS1 relies on PEX5 and can remain functional. This comparison is more informative than observing only one cargo.
numerical
A hypothetical cell supplies 160 precursors/min and has a saturated productive import capacity of 120/min. If no alternative loss occurs, how many unimported molecules accumulate over 5 min?
The excess rate is 160 − 120 = 40 molecules/min; multiplying by 5 min yields 200. The result assumes constant rates and no degradation.
numerical
An isolated organelle assay reaches a plateau of 60% of the starting pool. If the competent fraction follows first-order k = 0.2 min⁻¹, what percentage of the original pool is imported at t = 5 min?
The imported fraction is 0.60 × (1 − e^(−1)) = 0.3792, or about 37.9%. The remaining 40% is assumed incompetent. A plateau alone does not identify why that fraction is incompetent.
numerical
At steady state a shuttling reporter is 75% nuclear. If k_in = 0.15 min⁻¹, what is k_out under the simple two-pool model?
0.45 min⁻¹
0.20 min⁻¹
0.05 min⁻¹
N/C = 0.75/0.25 = 3 = k_in/k_out; k_out = 0.15/3 = 0.05 min⁻¹. Multiplying 0.75 by k_in is not the appropriate relationship.
analytical

A cell expressing a signal-deletion mutant has low total cargo and almost no mature organelle product. Briefly reducing precursor degradation reveals a cytosolic mutant band. Which explanation fits best?
The mutation necessarily prevents transcription
The protein is synthesized exclusively inside the organelle
Processing and protein degradation are identical events
Failed targeting may be followed by removal of mislocalized precursor

The appearance of cytosolic precursor when degradation is reduced supports synthesis followed by loss. It does not by itself specify the degradation machinery or prove that the signal deletion has no additional folding effects.
integrative

A ligand locks four reporters into stable folded domains without masking their signals: NLS, mitochondrial presequence, plastid stromal transit peptide, and PTS1. Which comparison is most reasonable for their canonical routes?
Mitochondrial and plastid envelope entry may be preferentially impaired; nuclear and peroxisomal routes can accommodate folded cargo
All four must stop equally because all membranes are lipid
Only the PTS1 reporter necessarily fails because Pex5 must unfold it
Only nuclear entry necessarily fails because pores accept solely unfolded chains

The canonical mitochondrial and plastid envelope systems require translocation-compatible cargo. Nuclear and peroxisomal import can admit folded proteins, although particular reporters and complexes may have size, accessibility or receptor limitations.
